crons.name: heartbeat
crons.prompt: cortextos bus update-cron-fire heartbeat --interval 4h 2>/dev/null; TASK_ID=$(cortextos bus create-task "Cron: heartbeat" --desc "Scheduled cron run" 2>/dev/null); cortextos bus update-task $TASK_ID in_progress 2>/dev/null; Read HEARTBEAT.md and follow its instructions. Update heartbeat, check inbox, run fleet health check across all 3 repos.

crons.name: repo-health
crons.prompt: cortextos bus update-cron-fire repo-health --interval 4h 2>/dev/null; TASK_ID=$(cortextos bus create-task "Cron: repo-health" --desc "Scheduled cron run" 2>/dev/null); cortextos bus update-task $TASK_ID in_progress 2>/dev/null; REPO HEALTH CHECK — Check git log --oneline -5 for each repo (~/code/clearpath, ~/code/lifecycle-killer, ~/code/nonprofit-hub, ~/code/auditos). Check Railway deploy status if any recent commits. Report anomalies to Josh via Telegram 6690120787. If all healthy, skip silently. Format: *Repo Health — [date]* with bullet list of issues. SILENT-OK if all healthy.

crons.name: upstream-sync
crons.prompt: TASK_ID=$(cortextos bus create-task "Cron: upstream-sync" --desc "Scheduled cron run" 2>/dev/null); cortextos bus update-task $TASK_ID in_progress 2>/dev/null; cortextos bus update-cron-fire upstream-sync --interval 7d 2>/dev/null; UPSTREAM SYNC CHECK — Run: cd /Users/joshweiss/cortextos && git fetch upstream. Check: git log --oneline HEAD..upstream/main | wc -l. If >0 commits pending: extract list (git log --oneline HEAD..upstream/main) and changed files (git diff HEAD..upstream/main --name-only). ALSO run: gh pr list --repo grandamenium/cortextos --state open (per P7 rule 3 — forks are invisible to branch scans, so this must run every time, not just when upstream/main has new commits). Telegram to 6690120787 with summary of pending commits, file categories (skills, dashboard, core, tests), and any open upstream PRs worth adopting. Reference .claude/orchestration-fleet-build/research/upstream-merge-conflict-map.md for conflict resolution strategy. NEVER auto-merge — present to Josh and wait for approval. SILENT-OK if up-to-date and no relevant open PRs.

crons.name: test-status
crons.prompt: TASK_ID=$(cortextos bus create-task "Cron: test-status" --desc "Scheduled cron run" 2>/dev/null); cortextos bus update-task $TASK_ID in_progress 2>/dev/null; cortextos bus update-cron-fire test-status --interval 24h 2>/dev/null; TEST STATUS — Run npm test in each active repo (~/code/clearpath, ~/code/lifecycle-killer, ~/code/nonprofit-hub, ~/code/auditos). crons.name: dependency-audit
crons.prompt: TASK_ID=$(cortextos bus create-task "Cron: dependency-audit" --desc "Scheduled cron run" 2>/dev/null); cortextos bus update-task $TASK_ID in_progress 2>/dev/null; cortextos bus update-cron-fire dependency-audit --interval 7d 2>/dev/null; DEPENDENCY AUDIT — For each repo (~/code/clearpath, ~/code/lifecycle-killer, ~/code/nonprofit-hub, ~/code/auditos): (1) npm audit — flag high/critical vulnerabilities. SILENT-OK if all PRs <4h old or no open PRs.

crons.name: kb-maintenance-sweep
crons.prompt: TASK_ID=$(cortextos bus create-task 'Cron: kb-maintenance-sweep' --desc 'Nightly Tier-1 KB content-health sweep (dead-link/orphan/junk/dup/freshness/canary) + findings' 2>/dev/null); cortextos bus update-task $TASK_ID in_progress 2>/dev/null; cortextos bus update-cron-fire kb-maintenance-sweep --interval 24h 2>/dev/null; NIGHTLY KB MAINTENANCE SWEEP (Tier 1, zero-LLM) — (1) Check the PREVIOUS run's row: tail -1 $CTX_AGENT_DIR/state/kb-maintenance-ledger.jsonl. If it is missing or has "green": false (a scan crashed), send Telegram 6690120787 with the row — silent failure on a KB cron is NOT acceptable. (2) Feed Tier-3 event marks from last night's reconcile: CHANGED=$(tail -1 $CTX_AGENT_DIR/state/kb-reconcile-ledger.jsonl | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(",".join((json.load(sys.stdin).get("reconcile") or {}).get("failed_paths",[]) or []))' 2>/dev/null). (3) Launch tonight's sweep in the BACKGROUND: run bash $CTX_AGENT_DIR/bin/kb-maintenance-sweep.sh --canary ${CHANGED:+--changed-files "$CHANGED"} as a background Bash call. It writes its own ledger row + a dated findings file under knowledge-sync/system/kb-maintenance/. (4) cortextos bus complete-task $TASK_ID --result 'kb-maintenance launched; previous night checked' 2>/dev/null. SILENT-OK if previous row green and launch succeeded. Do NOT auto-apply any finding — mechanical fixes route to auto-PR, merges/deletions/rewrites route to bus tasks for approval.

crons.name: kb-maintenance-digest
crons.prompt: TASK_ID=$(cortextos bus create-task 'Cron: kb-maintenance-digest' --desc 'Weekly KB content-health digest: Tier-2 LLM verify over Tier-1 candidates + ONE Telegram digest' 2>/dev/null); cortextos bus update-task $TASK_ID in_progress 2>/dev/null; cortextos bus update-cron-fire kb-maintenance-digest --interval 168h 2>/dev/null; WEEKLY KB MAINTENANCE DIGEST — (1) Run the Tier-2 verify layer over this week's Tier-1 candidates only (near-dup / staleness / contradiction / one-fact-one-home): export MMRAG_DIR="$HOME/.cortextos/${CTX_INSTANCE_ID:-default}/orgs/clearworksai/knowledge-base"; $CTX_REPO/knowledge-base/venv/bin/python3 $CTX_REPO/knowledge-base/scripts/kb_maintenance.py --tier all --dry-run > /tmp/kb-maint-weekly.json (LLM step is a documented stub unless KB_MAINT_ENABLE_LLM=1). (2) Summarize the week's findings files under knowledge-sync/system/kb-maintenance/ into ONE digest and send it to Telegram 6690120787 — one weekly digest, NOT per-item pings (comms doctrine). (3) For approval-required items (merges/deletions/rewrites/quarantine), create bus tasks assigned to larry with the finding file attached. (4) cortextos bus complete-task $TASK_ID --result 'weekly KB digest sent' 2>/dev/null.
